JUDGMENT
The private complaint (PCR No. 11830/12) filed by the complainant- Bidan Chandra Gupta.
This court referred the case to Malleswaram Police station to investigate U/s 156(3) of Cr.P.C.

The Malleswaram Police station registered the Cr. No. 124/2013 and The Police Sub Inspector of Malleswaram P.S has submitted the Charge Sheet against the accused for the offences punishable U/s. 467, 468, 471 , 201 and 420 of IPC.
C.C.27301/2014 2.

The brief facts of the Prosecution case are as follows:
It is alleged that the accused took loan of Rs.30 lakhs from Union Bank of India,
Chandra Layout Branch for purchasing flat No.202 in Begur Heights Apartment and the accused got registered the sale deed. Thereafter the accused failed to repay the bank loan amount and the possession of the house was taken by the bank.

The accused with an intention of cheating created another sale deed by forging the signature of the Sub Registrar on the sale deed and in turn sold the said house to C.W.1 and C.W.1 took loan in Axis Bank and paid Rs.24,50,000/- to the accused.

Thereby the accused has committed the offences punishable u/s 467, 468, 471, 201 and 420 of IPC.
3.

On the basis of the Statement of CW1, the Malleswaram Police have registered a case under Crime No.124/2013 for the offences punishable u/s 193, 200, 120B, 420 and 467 of IPC against the accused and submitted the FIR before the court.

Thereafter the investigating officer visited the spot and drawn the spot mahazar and recorded the statement of witnesses on completion of the investigation, the Charge Sheet has been filed against the accused for the offences punishable u/s 467, 468, 471, 201 and 420 of IPC.

In order to constitute an offence of cheating it has to be shown by the prosecution that there was some inducement on the part of the accused persons and that the said inducement was made fraudulently or dishonestly with a view to deceive the complainant.

It has also to be shown by the prosecution that due to the deception practiced by the accused persons, the person so deceived had delivered the property to the accused persons or had given consent that the accused persons shall retain the property.
Hence the concept of deception should exist from the very start of the transaction.
If that is wanting there would not be any criminal offence of cheating.

15. Now let us see with the available materials whether the prosecution would be able to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt to say that the accused has deceived the complainant fraudulently.

34. In the light of above evidence, the learned Sr.APP argued that there is evidence to believe that the act committed by the accused is nothing but cheating and there is sufficient material on record to convict the accused.
Therefore, he prayed to convict the accused.
35. The learned advocate for accused argued that, the material witnesses to the case of prosecution have not supported the case.
There is nothing on record to believe that accused has committed offences punishable U/s.467, 468, 471, 201 and 420 of IPC.
The prosecution has failed to prove the offences beyond reasonable doubt.
Hence prays this court to acquit the accused.

36. It is pertinent to note that the C.W.1/P.W.2 admitted that he was aware that the accused at the time of purchase, availed the housing loan from the Union Bank of India and the said house was mortgaged.

In the cross examination P.W.2 admitted that the Axis Bank had knowledge that the accused had availed loan on the said C.C.27301/2014 house at Union Bank before the loan was Bidhan Chndra Gupta vs B.T.Venkatesh on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164731133/

Moreover in ExD1 i.e, the sale deed at page No.5 it is mentioned as "
the purchaser has paid a sum of Rs. 30,00,000/- paid by way of DD No. 001790 dated 31-03-2009 drawn on union bank of India Bangalore.
The loan amount sanctioned by Union Bank of India Bengaluru.
The vendor has acknowledge the receipt of the same"
Therefore in the sale deed it is specifically mentioned about taking loan by the accused from the Union Bank.

It is also very clear from the evidence of P.W.2/complainant that himself and AXIS Bank were aware about the loan taken by the accused in Union Bank of India and the original documents were in the custody of AXIS Bank.

37. It is pertinent to note that the prosecution failed to mark the sanction letter, mortgage deed of Union Bank of India or a statement to show that the accused is defaulter in repayment of the loan.
There is no evidence on record to show that the accused made unlawful gain by cheating the Union Bank.
. The prosecution has not produced the original sale deed dated 17.04.2009 executed by Sri.Ravi Kumar in favor of the accused and also not produced the alleged fabricated sale deed.

The prosecution has not made any efforts to send the original and fabricated sale Deed to FSL for expert opinion and failed to establish that the accused created a fraudulent sale deed with an intention to deceive C.W.1.

The Sub-Registrar (C.W.8) who was present at the time of registration of the sale deed dated 17.04.2009 is not examined and as such there is no evidence to establish that the signature and seal of C.W.8 was forged by the accused.
39. It is relevant to note that during trial the prosecution filed an application permitting to lead further investigation U/Sec. 173(8) of Cr.P.C and to produce the alleged fraudulent sale deed.

The application dated 22.02.2019 was dismissed by the Court and again another application filed by the prosecution U/s 242(2) of Cr.P.C. seeking permission of this court to produce the original sale Deed.
This court dismissed the application.
Against the order the complainant has preferred criminal revision petition before the Hon'ble session court at Bengaluru.
The criminal Revision Petition C.C.27301/2014 has also been dismissed.
Hence no original documents has been got marked on behalf of the prosecution to prove the forgery.

40. In the absence of the fraudulent sale deed no case is made out and the offence U/s 420 IPC being a consequential one cannot sustain and the prosecution failed to establish that the accused has created fraudulent document and the accused by using the fraudulent document deceived the C.W.1 to purchase the property thereby the offences U/s 467, 468, 471 and 420 are not made out.
